tasks.short: Change security files and individual access status

steps.what: Submit a request to change access status
Check computer security files for errors
Sign the individual access status change
Apply the signed access status
Correct errors that name no software

tasks.design: The user submits account id, system id, software id and the requested access status on a {WORKFLOW} form tied to a {HELPDESK} ticket. The security analyst signs one status version. The {DATA_PLATFORM} writes that version into the security file. Rows with no software id stay on a manual list.
tasks.previous_blocker: Access requests arrived by mail with no stable account id, so a job could not know which security file to change.
tasks.enabler_now: The directory and the request form can share an account id, a software id and a status value.
tasks.still_hard: A wrong status on a privileged account is costly, and some errors do not match a software id.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst signs the individual access status, and corrects by hand any error the rule cannot name.

ambition.what: Clear access status requests in the same week, not in a monthly queue

tasks.altitude: Clean requests take less retyping. The analyst can refuse a status change that has no signed version.

reach.task: Use only the access status the analyst signed
reach.learn: Which request ids were applied and which are waiting on an error

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm, changing a security file is a request plus a directory update. The judgement is whether that person's status should change.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. An access log should record account id, status and actor, not how the person works.
Digest [S16] says Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and includes a duty of care. Sector and size decide whether a firm is in scope.
Digest [S28] reports a coding agent that deleted a production database despite instructions, so no agent changes an access file by itself.

assumptions: Focal role is the security analyst. The task changes a security file only after a signed status version. It does not score the person and it does not watch how they work.
Input contract: account id, system id, software id, requested access status, ticket id, requester. Producer is the system user. If the software id or account id is missing the row is not applied.
Use the directory's own access-update job before custom code. The prior meeting share overstates this task: the decision is a short review, and the rest is the security file.
unknowns: Who may sign a privileged status when the analyst is absent.
Which accounts have no software id.
Whether joiners and leavers already arrive from the staff record.
research_questions: What share of access requests has no software id?
How many status changes are reversed in the same week?

already_counted.description: Analyst reviews the diff before signing the status
Analyst time correcting errors by hand

incremental.description: Add software ids when a new system joins the directory
Users resubmit requests the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: access status version for this request id
the same signed access status version
error correction signed for this security file

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes many requests lack an account id, so the analyst still edits the security file by hand. The high case assumes clean requests apply after a signature, while every odd error stays manual. No unattended writes.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review violations and discuss them with violators

steps.what: Read violations of security procedures
Prepare the violators case note from fields

loop.input: violation id, procedure id, account id and event time
loop.output: case note that copies only those fields
loop.check: Every field in the note is present on the event
loop.stop: If the procedure id is missing, return the raw row and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Procedure names vary and a fixed sentence cannot explain the event

steps.what: Decide which violations need a discussion
Discuss procedures with the violators
Record that repeated violations were discussed

tasks.design: A security event already holds violation id, procedure id, account id and event time on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A bounded note in {DOCS} copies those fields and nothing else. The security analyst discusses procedures with the violator in person. The note does not score the person, and the design adds no new watch of staff.
tasks.previous_blocker: Violation notes were rewritten from console screenshots, so the conversation started without a stable procedure id.
tasks.enabler_now: The event record already has the fields the note needs, so the draft does not have to infer them.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a violation was a mistake or a repeat, and how to say that to the person, is a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst decides which violations need a talk, and holds that talk. The machine does not speak for them.

ambition.what: Discuss a repeated violation in the same week, not at the next quarterly review

tasks.altitude: Less time rebuilding the case from screenshots. The conversation and the decision to hold it stay with the analyst.

reach.task: Follow the procedure discussed in the meeting
reach.learn: Which procedure ids were discussed and which events are still open

evidence.claim: Reviewing a violation and talking with the person is meeting work. A prepared note can shorten the start. It cannot replace the talk.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. The note uses the event already stored, not a wider watch of the person.
Digest [S23] says a works council is consulted before staff monitoring. Discussing a recorded violation with the violator is a person conversation, not a new monitor and not a score.

assumptions: Focal role is the security analyst. The task ends when the conversation outcome is written. No model scores the violator. No new staff-monitoring view is built.

Input contract: violation id, procedure id, account id, event time, system id. Producer is the existing security event. If the procedure id is missing the analyst works from the raw row and does not use the note.
Use the document store's own note template before custom code. Works-council consent applies if someone later asks for a named-person dashboard. This design does not.
unknowns: Whether the works council has already agreed the existing security log.
Who meets the violator when the analyst is absent.
Which events are duplicates of an older case.
research_questions: What share of violations has no procedure id?
How often is the same account in a violation again within a quarter?

already_counted.description: Analyst edits the case note before the talk
The conversation itself stays with the analyst

incremental.description: Keep the note template aligned when procedure ids change

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most events lack a procedure id, so the note stays empty and the analyst still prepares by hand. The high case assumes the note is clean, while every decision and every conversation stays manual. No automated sanction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Document security policies procedures and tests

steps.what: Gather emergency measures and tests
Draft policies and procedures from field ids

loop.input: procedure id, test id and emergency measure id
loop.output: headings each tagged to an id
loop.check: Every filled heading cites an id from the source list
loop.stop: One pass; a heading with no id stays blank
loop.why_not_simpler: Procedure sentences are not a field copy and must stay with the analyst

steps.what: Sign the security procedures document
File the signed policies and tests
Tell owners which document was filed

tasks.design: Test id, procedure id and emergency measure id arrive on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded draft in {DOCS} fills headings and those ids only. The security analyst writes the procedure prose and signs the document version. {DOCS} files that signed version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policies were rewritten from old files, and test results lived in mail, so a draft could not show which test a sentence relied on.
tasks.enabler_now: Completed tests and procedures can be named with stable ids that a heading can cite.
tasks.still_hard: The sentences that say what people must do are still the analyst's, and a metadata fill is the wrong tool for them.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst writes the measures and procedures, and signs the document version that others will follow.

ambition.what: File the procedures document in the week a test result is renewed, not at the annual rewrite

tasks.altitude: Less time on headings and version chores. The analyst keeps the right to refuse a document whose procedures cite no test.

reach.task: Follow the signed procedures for their system
reach.learn: Which procedure ids and test ids the current document cites

evidence.claim: Writing security procedures is document work. Headings and ids can be copied. The instructions themselves are not a lookup.
Digest [S3] says a document prompt can fill metadata and the fill can be wrong, so this draft copies headings and ids only, not the procedure prose.
Digest [S16] and [S18] say Dutch cyber law has been in force since 15 August 2026 and includes a duty of care for firms in scope. Scope depends on sector and size. The document is not proof of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the security analyst. The task ends when the signed policies document is filed. Running the tests is a different task.

Input contract: procedure id, test id, emergency measure id, system id, owner. Producer is the service owner. If an id is missing that heading stays blank and the analyst writes it by hand or leaves it out.
Use the document store's own templates and version history before custom code. Do not use a metadata fill for the procedure sentences.
unknowns: Who may sign a policy when the analyst is absent.
Which procedures have no test id.
Whether this firm must keep the document for a duty of care.
research_questions: What share of procedures cites no test from the last year?
How often does the signed document differ from the last test result?

already_counted.description: Analyst writes the procedure sentences the headings do not cover
Analyst sign-off time on the document

incremental.description: Revise headings when a new emergency measure type is added
Service owners resubmit test ids the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: policy document version signed in this review
the same signed policy document version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most procedures arrive as free text with no ids, so the draft stays blank and the analyst still writes the document. The high case assumes headings fill, while every procedure sentence and every sign-off stays with the analyst. The tests themselves are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Confer with users on access and programming changes

steps.what: Mail issues on computer data access
Prepare confer notes from open tickets

loop.input: ticket id, access need, violation id and programming change id
loop.output: confer note listing those fields only
loop.check: Each id on the note is present on the ticket
loop.stop: If the ticket id is missing, return an empty note and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: Mail wording does not split into access, violation and programming change by a fixed table

steps.what: Confer on access issues and programming changes
Write the outcome of the confer
Confirm the access needs with the user

tasks.design: The user sends a {HELPDESK} ticket, often by {EMAIL}, with an access need, a violation id and a programming change id. A bounded note in {DOCS} lists those fields and does not invent others. The security analyst confers in person. The outcome is a short note, not a system change and not a score of the user.
tasks.previous_blocker: User issues arrived as long mail with no ticket id, so similar access needs and programming changes did not line up.
tasks.enabler_now: A ticket can carry an access need, a violation id and a programming change id as separate fields.
tasks.still_hard: What the user actually needs, and whether a programming change is in scope, comes out in the conversation.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst confers with the user and decides which issues to accept. The note only prepares that talk.

ambition.what: Hold the user conference in the week the access issue arrives, not at a monthly surgery

tasks.altitude: Less time reconstructing the mail. The conference stays the analyst's, and no access change is made in the meeting.

reach.task: Pick up programming changes the analyst wrote down
reach.learn: Which change ids were agreed and which access needs are still open

evidence.claim: Conferring with users about access and changes is meeting work. A fielded ticket can prepare it. The talk itself does not become a record on its own.
Digest [S22] says security logging must stay necessary and proportionate. The confer note copies ticket fields only, and does not add a watch of the user.

assumptions: Focal role is the security analyst. The task ends at the outcome note. Applying an access change or editing code is a different task. The user is not scored.

Input contract: ticket id, access need, violation id, programming change id, system id. Producer is the system user. If the ticket id is missing the analyst confers from the mail and marks the note manual.
Use the ticket form's own fields before custom code. The prior screen share is the ticket, not a build. The meeting stays in person.
unknowns: Whether programming changes belong to this analyst or to a developer.
Which tickets mix several issues in one free-text field.
Who covers the conference when the analyst is away.
research_questions: What share of user mail has no ticket id?
How often does the conference agree a programming change rather than an access need?

already_counted.description: Analyst corrects a confer note before the meeting
The conference itself stays with the analyst

incremental.description: Adjust ticket fields when a new issue type appears
Users resubmit tickets that lack an issue type

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most issues stay as free-text mail, so the note rarely fires and the analyst still prepares by hand. The high case assumes clean tickets, while every conference and every outcome stays manual. No access change is treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The analyst stops retyping access rows and policy headings, and keeps the time for status decisions, violation talks and user conferences.
reach: System users receive a signed access status or a short outcome from the conference, not a silent change.
Service owners receive the filed procedures document and can see which tests it cites.
skills_to_grow: State an access change as an account, a status and a signed version.
Prepare a violation note from fields already on the record, then talk.
Keep procedure prose in the signed document, not in a metadata fill.
Take a user issue as access, a violation or a programming change before the conference.
role.ambitious_version: Access changes and policy versions are signed, and every violation or user issue still ends in a conversation.
